q: This recipe is my version of the famous aubergine and tomato salad called zaalouk, one of the best of all cooked Moroccan salads. Utterly delicious on slices of warm Berber Griddle Breads (page 110), zaalouk will keep for several days in the refrigerator, getting better and better.
2012, Paula Wolfert, The Food of Morocco:
Z (zaa): a loose-tongued z; same as above.
2006, Coleman South, Leslie Jermyn, Syria, page 95:
the letter Zaa, formally an emphatic 'z', but often pronounced as an emphatic 'd' in Egyptian Arabic
2013, Jane Wightwick, Mahmoud Gaafar, Colloquial Arabic of Egypt:

e: From Arabic زَعْتَر (zaʕtar), صَعْتَر (ṣaʕtar, “wild thyme; condiment made from this herb”), probably from Classical Syriac ܨܬܪܐ (ṣāṯrā), related to Hebrew צַתְרָה (ṣátrā).
